- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is significantly below recent highs, adjust upward by 2–5% to capture momentum.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and forecast is above recent lows, reduce forecast by 3–7% to avoid overcorrection.
- If forecast shows sharp upward spike followed by rapid decline, reduce subsequent forecast values by 10–20% to account for volatility decay.
- If forecast mean is consistently 5–10% above true outcome over 30-day horizon, apply downward bias correction by 1–3% per day for the next 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., 1–2 days of +1.00 then -0.30), reduce forecast volatility by 15–25% to avoid overfitting to noise.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >10% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with 14-day trend unless sentiment strongly contradicts it.
